Tips for sharing

  • Send it from the school's usual account or newsletter, so families recognise it.
  • Share it at a natural moment: the start of term, or before birthdays and Christmas.
  • Put printed copies where parents wait, such as by the school gate or reception.
Why the posters are worded the way they are

Each poster is written so that it encourages families, rather than putting them off. If you change the wording, please keep to these:

  • From the school, not from us. Families trust their school. The poster is signed by the headteacher, and names a member of staff to ask.
  • One clear ask, and an easy first step. Each poster asks for one thing and gives three small steps, so families know exactly what to do this week.
  • The family's choice, not an order. No "must" or "ban". Warnings and pressure make some families, and many children, do the opposite.
  • What families are doing, not what they're not. It says that families across 80 schools are taking part. It never says how many children have phones, which would make having one seem normal.
  • Thanks, not blame. It thanks families and children for helping, and doesn't make anyone feel judged for the phone they have.
